entries.claim: Range arithmetic is unchecked, so a malformed negative turn offset or length can panic or address the wrong blocks instead of failing that range.
entries.failure_scenario: The readers cast `stream_offset` and `byte_len` from `i64` to `u64` before calling `archive::ranges`. If a damaged turn row contains `stream_offset = -1` and a positive length, `offset + len` overflows here: debug builds panic, while optimized builds wrap `end` and subsequent `end - start` arithmetic can underflow or select invalid slice bounds. Thus search, get, context, or brief can crash on malformed archive coordinates rather than leaving only that turn unread.

counter_evidence.note: Half true. `let end = offset + len` at archive.rs:105 is unchecked and runs before `reader.blocks(offset, len)?` at :107, so a negative stream_offset cast to u64 panics there in a debug or test build. The wrong-blocks and invalid-slice claims are false: the span pass at :71-73 drops any range blocks() rejects, and blocks() (blob/block.rs:253-258) uses checked_add and returns RangeOutOfBounds before the wrapped `end` is ever used, so a release build (no overflow-checks in [profile.release]) fails only that range. Low: a debug-only panic on a corrupt turn row.
